name: STONEX GROUP INC

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The counter is that I am explaining away a real warning. 5.01x tangible book is genuinely expensive for a business whose earnings are cyclical, transaction-volume dependent and levered to volatility that will not stay elevated forever. StoneX's returns are flattered by a period of exceptional commodity and rates volatility; normalise volatility and the 17.6% ROTCE falls toward the low teens, at which point a 1.85x-2.5x justified multiple is about right and the stock is worth a third of its price. The 'compounder deserves a premium' argument is exactly what people say at the top of a cycle, and the stock is already down 10.6% over 21 days, which may be the market starting to agree.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: ROTCE through a low-volatility quarter. If StoneX's returns hold in the high teens when commodity and rates volatility normalises, the compounder case is intact; if they compress into the low teens, the model's justified multiple is closer to right than my objection to it.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Only ambiguously. Net income has risen in each of the last three years, which supports the compounder reading, but those three years were all high-volatility years, so the series does not test the counter at all. The 21-day 10.6% drawdown is price action, not evidence. I could not find a low-volatility period inside the window to observe, which means the strongest bear argument here is untested rather than refuted.
devils_advocate.unresolved: Whether StoneX's ROTCE survives a normal-volatility environment — the single question that decides whether 5x tangible book is a premium for compounding or a peak-cycle multiple. I also could not separate RJO's contribution from the legacy business in the fiscal 2026 results, so I cannot say whether the acquisition is accretive to returns or diluting them.

what_changed: The R.J. O'Brien acquisition closed on 31 July 2025, inside StoneX's fiscal 2025 (year end 30 September 2025) and therefore inside the three-year ROTCE window the model averages. Equity value was approximately $900 million: about $610.6 million of cash consideration reflecting RJO's tangible book above an agreed benchmark, plus 3,085,554 shares reissued from treasury against a pre-close target value of $275.0 million, with up to $143 million of RJO debt assumed. StoneX priced $625 million of secured notes to fund the cash portion. The 2026-08-05 8-K (item 2.02) carried fiscal Q3 results and there is a 2026-08-28 8-K under item 7.01. The extract shows the footprint of the deal clearly: equity jumped from $1,709.1M to $2,377.4M in a single year while goodwill and intangibles reached $730.2M, or 31% of book.
consensus_case: At $68.48 against $13.66 of tangible book, StoneX trades at 5.01x tangible common equity, and the market pays that because StoneX is a compounder, not a balance-sheet lender. Net income has run $238.5M, $260.8M and $305.9M across the last three years and book value has compounded at a high-teens to twenty percent rate for a decade. The business is a fee-and-spread franchise — clearing, execution, market-making across commodities, FX, securities and payments — where the balance sheet is a means of carrying client float rather than the source of earnings. Having just closed R.J. O'Brien, StoneX is the largest non-bank futures commission merchant in the United States and has added nearly $6 billion of client float. A buyer paying 5x tangible book for a franchise that grows book at 15-20% and earns high-teens returns is paying roughly 20x earnings for a business with scale advantages, which is not obviously rich.
base_case_rationale: This is a book-method name, so no FCFF growth applies and record.py does not reprice it. On the substance, I do not accept the model's −63.2% 'expensive' reading as a finding. The justified P/TBV of 1.85x comes from a Gordon-style relationship between a sustainable ROTCE of 17.6%, a cost of equity of 10.7% and the engine's fixed 2.5% terminal growth constant. That construction structurally undervalues any firm that reinvests at high returns and grows book value far faster than 2.5%: it capitalises the spread between return and cost of equity while assuming the capital base is nearly static. StoneX has grown book at roughly 15-20% a year. Feed a 2.5% growth constant into a business compounding equity at 15% and the model will call it expensive at almost any price, which is what has happened here. Separately, the 17.6% 'sustainable' ROTCE averages three years that straddle the RJO close — pre-deal years with a smaller, cleaner equity base against a post-deal year carrying $730M of goodwill and intangibles and a $625M notes issuance. That is the acquisition-inside-the-window problem LESSONS records for UMBF, in the ROTCE numerator rather than the book denominator. Neither the multiple nor the return input is trustworthy enough to support a directional call.
key_risks: 5.01x tangible book leaves no margin for a normalisation in commodity, rates and FX volatility
Earnings are transaction-volume dependent and the three-year record spans only high-volatility years
Goodwill and intangibles are 31% of book after RJO, so reported book quality has fallen
The RJO integration is roughly one year old and its return contribution is not yet separable
watch_for: ROTCE in a quarter with normalised volatility — the observable that settles the bull and bear cases
Segment disclosure separating RJO's contribution from the legacy FCM business
Client float and interest income sensitivity if short rates fall
